newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures close sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures close sharply lower.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed sharply lower after Standard & Poor's 500s plunged in the last hour of pit trade.
March S&Ps fell the 15-point intermediate price limit after the U.S. bond futures market closed the day on the downside, even though the Federal Reserve did not raise interest rates, traders said.

They said S&Ps were trading in fast-market conditions a half-hour before the contract dipped to 778.70, down 15 points. Likewise, March Nasdaq 100s plummeted more than 40.00 to 884.00, near their intermediate down limit of 45.00 points.

Arbitrage sell programs were noted in the S&P pit when March rose anywhere between 2.00 points and 0.80 point over cash, traders said. Fair value was at 2.80 points over, and arbitrage buy programs were at a 3.85 point premium.
They also said heavy sell-stop orders were touched at 787.20.
S&P futures trade was halted for two minutes at 1430 CST/2030 GMT because March remained offered at the 778.70 level, the 15-point lower limit, floor traders said.
Once the S&Ps re-opened, the contract immediately fell more than 6.00 points to the daily low of 771.50.
Nikkei 225 futures largely remained unaffected by the selling frenzy in the S&P pit. While March Nikkeis were lower, the contract held above support at 18,100.0.
Traders said the declines in U.S. technology stocks also contributed to the market's poor performance in the afternoon.
The activity in the afternoon contrasted with the placid pace of trade in the morning part of the session. Most traders were on the sidelines ahead of the FOMC meeting.
Despite the weak tone in the U.S. bond market, some bond analysts said the market represented good value to both foreign and domestic investors.
"We've seen a marked move out of stocks and into bonds by some of our investors," one bond market analyst said.

At the end of pit trade, March S&Ps were down 13.20 at 780.50, Value Lines were off 10.00 at 699.90, NYSE Composites were 6.40 points lower at 409.35, Nikkeis were 120.0 lower at 18,220, Midcap 400s were off 4.25 at 261.90 and Nasdaq 100s were down 28.25 at 896.50.
